correctness.rationale: The explicit 120/336/228-cell cubical model computes the continuous two-point space by the standard graph-configuration deformation retraction. The degree-one and degree-two signed boundaries square to zero; rational rank of degree two is at least 208 by exact F3 elimination and at most 208 from twenty independent genuine torus cycles. A signed 20x20 coordinate minor is -1, hence these cycles are a primitive rank-20 lattice. Since the kernel of a map between free abelian groups is primitive, they form its full integral lattice. Exact SNF of the 336x228 boundary is 1 repeated 207 times and 2 once. The cubical 1-skeleton is connected. The enumeration checks graph girth 6, all 24 six-cycles, 60 disjoint pairs, and all 96 automorphisms partitioning the pairs into 12 and 48. Both programs executed from the current package source with outputs retained; no finite sampling purports to prove a broader family. Dependencies and the topological model are explicit.

originality.rationale: The proposed new statement is a primitive integral basis of shortest-pair product tori for the nonplanar Möbius–Kantor two-point configuration space. Foundational papers study the general ordered deleted product, mature-graph ranks, or first braid homology, while the planar generation theorem explicitly excludes nonplanar graphs. The same-graph Möbius–Kantor paper studies graph geometry and its ordinary Lefschetz fixed-point theory, not point configurations. Closest searchable published records concern the same graph with other simplicial constructions, or analogous two-particle configuration homology on different graphs. None of the inspected theorem statements or matching published-finding corpus abstracts imply the specified 60 shortest geometric generators and -1 unimodular basis. Search is not a proof of priority; residual indexing and full-text risks remain.
residual_risks: Equivalent unpublished or poorly indexed work on two-particle Möbius–Kantor graph may exist.
The sections outside the inspected ranges of foundational lengthy papers were not read line by line; the theorem statements and explicit scopes supplied the non-implication comparison.

value.rationale: Integral generators represented by geometrically minimal disjoint-cycle motions are relevant to graph braid groups and the literature specifically asks for combinatorial second-homology bases. The Möbius–Kantor graph is a canonical nonplanar symmetric 8_3 incidence graph. That precisely its girth-six cycles suffice integrally, with an explicit 20-element primitive basis from 60 carriers and two symmetry orbits, is not a routine consequence of Euler characteristic, Betti-number tables, or first homology torsion. It supplies a reusable exact test object for nonplanar toric-generation questions without claiming an infinite-family theorem.
